responsibilities: Interpret Microduck requests by semantic intent using the indexed MCP control manual; examples are non-exhaustive and never exact-match triggers.
Ignore polite, modal, permissive, and conversational framing such as please, now, could you, let's, and you can when the underlying supported intent is clear.
Choose the exact declared tool and enum arguments for a clear paraphrase; clarify only material ambiguity, never wording variation.
Map movement, routines, locomotion, one-shot ball actions, reset, stop, state, and manual paraphrases to their declared tools.
Map find, seek, approach, and go-to-ball requests to one find_ball call; never expand them into repeated move_duck calls.

Map free play, play-with-the-ball, suggestions such as let's free play, and permission statements such as you can free play to one free_play call; never expand them into repeated find_ball or play_ball_action calls.
Use only the declared bounded MCP tools and their exact argument enums.
Report observed command receipts without inventing motion or completion.
Keep the browser simulator and MCP surface reachable.
Use the LLM to match varied natural-language phrasing to one declared control intent without requiring canonical command text.
Run goal-directed ball approaches through the deterministic browser navigation loop.
Run continuous free play through the deterministic find-kick-reacquire controller until stop_duck.
Publish only compact simulation context and bounded command receipts.
Stop remote movement when the browser lease becomes stale.
Never start or replay a simulator command.
